reviewed.topic: Which record consumes a credit, and when
reviewed.note: Deterministic: a credit is consumed only inside the finalization transaction of the record that exceeds the allowance (ordered by createdAt,id), never at session open/reservation. consumeEvidenceCreditForCompletion has exactly one caller (settlement); no route attaches a credit to an arbitrary existing record. Unique ledger evidence_id makes retries idempotent; conditional decrement (credits >= 1) prevents double-spend.

findings.title: An unsealed reservation stops counting after 24h but can still be finalized, and settlement only counts EARLIER records, so FREE/PRO allowances can be exceeded without a credit
findings.userImpact: Commercial: a FREE account can obtain more than 3 plan-funded records (and the paid outputs they earn) with no credit; the same applies to PRO's lifetime cap and TEAM's rolling window.
findings.reproduction: FREE account, 0 credits. T0: POST /v1/evidence x3 (records A,B,C, left unsealed). Keep each record's updated_at fresh (e.g. PATCH /v1/evidence/:id/label daily) so expiredEvidenceReservationWhere (requires updatedAt < now-24h) never releases them. T0+25h: countedEvidenceRecordWhere no longer counts A,B,C (unsealed and createdAt older than EVIDENCE_RESERVATION_TTL_MS) so admission sees 0 -> POST /v1/evidence x3 (D,E,F) admitted. Complete D,E,F first: settlement counts only slot-holding records created BEFORE each (createdBeforeEvidence); A,B,C are not slot-holding -> priors 0,1,2 -> funding PLAN. Then complete A,B,C: no slot-holding record was created before A, so priors are 0,1,2 -> PLAN. Result: 6 PLAN-funded records on FREE, repeatable. completeEvidence refuses only deletedAt!=null, never an aged reservation. Intake links have the same shape: a live intake session holds the record out of the sweep (reservation.ts:99) for the link's whole lifetime.
findings.observed: Admission population is time-windowed for unsealed records; completion has no reservation-age check; settlement counts only records created earlier than the one being settled.
findings.expected: A record that is finalized must be funded against the same population that admitted it: either an aged reservation cannot be finalized without re-admission, or settlement counts every slot-holding record regardless of creation order.
findings.rootCause: The 24h TTL was added to the COUNT (so abandoned reservations free their slot) without adding the matching refusal at COMPLETION, while settlement's 'prior records' cursor assumes every earlier record is already counted.
findings.remediation: In settleEvidenceCompletionFunding, count all slot-holding records other than this one (excludeEvidenceId) for the lifetime cap instead of createdBefore, OR at completion refuse/re-admit a record whose reservation is older than EVIDENCE_RESERVATION_TTL_MS (treat it as expired and require a fresh admission under the capacity lock).
findings.requiredTests: Integration: FREE user, 3 aged unsealed + 3 fresh records, finalize in both orders; assert at most 3 PLAN fundings and the rest 402/credit-consumed.
findings.runtimeProbe: Disposable PG: create FREE user; insert 3 Evidence rows status=UPLOADING createdAt=now-25h updatedAt=now with stored parts; call createEvidence x3 (expect success); call completeEvidence on the 3 new then the 3 old with a fake signer/TSA; count evidence_credit_ledger_entries (expect 0) and SIGNED records (6).

findings.title: Personal records are admitted under the 'personal:<owner>' capacity lock but settled under 'team:<personalTeamId>'; the monthly settlement population also omits legacy NULL-team rows
findings.userImpact: Creation and completion are not mutually serialized for Personal subjects, contrary to the ET-ACQ-06 comment; TEAM-plan personal settlement counts a narrower population than admission.
findings.reproduction: createEvidence resolves scope with teamId null for a personal capture (evidence.service.ts:404-407) -> getPersonalWorkspaceScope teamId:null (workspace-billing.service.ts:236) -> lock key personal:<owner>. completeEvidence resolves with teamId = evidence.teamId (the personal Team id, never null since HOME-DATA-OWNERSHIP) -> getTeamWorkspaceScope teamId=<personalTeam> -> lock key team:<personalTeam>. Settlement's monthly branch then counts teamId=<personalTeam> only (855-865) while admission counts NULL + personal team (298-300).
findings.observed: Two different advisory-lock keys and two different monthly populations for the same commercial subject.
findings.expected: lockEvidenceCapacitySubject and the monthly count key on the commercial principal (billingShape SINGLE_OCCUPANT -> owner), identically at both phases.
findings.rootCause: Lock key and monthly population are derived from scope.teamId, which differs by builder, rather than from the billing shape.
findings.remediation: Key the lock and the rolling-window count on commercialPrincipalOf(scope) (SINGLE_OCCUPANT -> personal:<owner>).
findings.requiredTests: Unit: both scope builders for one personal record yield the same lock key.

findings.title: One banked credit admits any number of over-allowance reservations; all but one fail with 402 at completion after the bytes were uploaded
findings.userImpact: A FREE user at 3/3 with 1 credit can start several captures (e.g. a continuous screen recording) that are admitted, fully uploaded, and then refused INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE_CREDITS at seal; the capture is stranded until the 24h sweep.
findings.legalImpact: A capture the user believed was being preserved is not sealed.
findings.reproduction: FREE, 3 records, credits=1. Open two direct-capture sessions and reserve both: both admissions see count>=3 and credits>=1 -> allowed. Upload and seal both: the first consumes the credit, the second throws 402 INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE_CREDITS inside completion.
findings.observed: Admission checks wallet balance but not credits already committed to open over-allowance reservations.
findings.expected: Admission should subtract live over-allowance reservations from available credits (or refuse with a clear 'credit already committed' code) so an admitted capture can complete.
findings.rootCause: Deliberate 'admission only, spend at completion' design without a pending-commitment count.
findings.remediation: In assertWorkspaceAllowsEvidenceCreation compare credits against (slot-holding count - allowance) instead of >=1.
findings.requiredTests: FREE+1 credit, two concurrent reservations: second admission refused.

findings.title: Active entitlement is check-then-create with no uniqueness, so concurrent first requests can create two active entitlements and the wallet/plan readers disagree
findings.userImpact: A purchased credit or plan can land on one row while another reader (findFirst without orderBy) reads the other.
findings.reproduction: ensureEntitlement / auth.service findFirst({userId, active:true}) then create; schema has only @@index([userId]) and no migration adds a unique index. Two parallel first requests insert two rows. consumeEvidenceCreditForCompletion uses updateMany({userId, active, credits>=1}) and requires count===1.
findings.observed: No DB invariant of one active entitlement per user.
findings.expected: Partial unique index on entitlements(user_id) WHERE active.
findings.rootCause: Invariant held only by application check-then-create.
findings.remediation: Add partial unique index (with a dedupe migration) and upsert.
findings.runtimeProbe: Disposable PG: Promise.all 10x ensureEntitlement(newUser); count active rows.

findings.title: Resumable-upload byte-write routes (part presign, parts/uploaded, multipart/complete, complete) authorize on team membership only; another member can write bytes into a colleague's in-flight evidence
findings.userImpact: A same-workspace member holding the session id can overwrite parts of a colleague's multipart upload; the bridge then attaches the object to the colleague's record as the colleague, and finalization signs it.
findings.legalImpact: A sealed record attributed to one person can contain bytes supplied by another; custody says the owner uploaded them.
findings.securityImpact: Intra-tenant evidence tampering before seal (requires the session UUID; no cross-tenant path because every query is team-scoped).
findings.reproduction: Member A (owner) opens POST /v1/uploads/sessions for her record (web uploader sends no expectedSha256, apps/web/lib/uploads/multipart-uploader.ts). Member B of the same team (evidence.create) calls POST /v1/uploads/sessions/<sid>/parts/0/presign {teamId} -> presignStorageUploadPart loads the session by (teamId, sessionId) only and returns an S3 part URL; B PUTs his bytes and calls /parts/0/uploaded with his ETag (markPartUploaded is team-scoped and COALESCEs client_sha256); B or A calls /multipart/complete -> completeStorageMultipart (team-scoped) -> bridge writeEvidencePart as principal session.actor_user_id (A). A's finalize hashes and signs B's bytes.
findings.observed: Only createUploadSession and abortUploadSession check actor/owner (ET-UPL-01/02); presign, parts/uploaded, multipart/initiate, multipart/complete and complete do not.
findings.expected: Every session mutation requires the caller to be the session's actor (or the record owner), answering like an unknown session otherwise.
findings.rootCause: ET-UPL-01 fix moved the bridge to the byte-write authority as the SESSION's actor, not the CALLER; per-route caller checks were added only to create/abort.
findings.remediation: Add actorUserId to presignStorageUploadPart/markPartUploaded/initiate/completeStorageMultipart/completeUploadSession inputs and require actor_user_id = caller in the loading query.
findings.requiredTests: Two members of one team; B's presign/uploaded/multipart-complete on A's session -> 404 session_not_found.
findings.runtimeProbe: Disposable API+PG+minio: team with users A,B; A creates evidence + upload session + initiate; B calls presign with A's sessionId; assert 200 today (defect) vs 404 expected.

findings.title: The browser extension's origin is not allowed by the API CORS policy in production and the extension has no host_permissions, so Direct Web Capture depends on an undocumented CORS_ORIGINS entry
findings.userImpact: In production every extension API call (bearer + JSON => preflight) and the S3 presigned PUT fail CORS unless an operator has added chrome-extension://<id> to CORS_ORIGINS and the bucket CORS; nothing in the repo does or documents it.
findings.reproduction: Origin chrome-extension://<32 chars> is not in allowedWebOrigins, not matched by isProovraOrigin (*.proovra.com, *.vercel.app), and isProd blocks the fallthrough; manifest host_permissions is [] so the MV3 service worker fetch is CORS-bound. CORS_ORIGINS is empty in services/api/.env.example and all workflows; no infra file configures S3 bucket CORS.
findings.observed: No source or doc path admits the extension origin.
findings.expected: Pinned extension origin (the same id as EXTENSION_OAUTH_REDIRECT_ALLOW) accepted explicitly, or host_permissions for the API/storage origins in the manifest, plus documented bucket CORS.
findings.rootCause: UC-1 added OAuth redirect pinning but not the matching CORS/host-permission wiring.
findings.remediation: Derive an allowed chrome-extension://<id> origin from the pinned extension id config; add host_permissions for api and storage origins at build time; document bucket CORS.
findings.requiredTests: CORS preflight from chrome-extension://<pinned id> with NODE_ENV=production -> Access-Control-Allow-Origin echoed; unpinned id -> absent.

findings.title: Every API request log line writes the raw URL; only invite tokens are redacted, so intake-link tokens, external-review access tokens, org-invite tokens and public verify share tokens reach the logs
findings.userImpact: Anyone with log access (and every log sink/backup) can replay an intake link (upload into the org's workspace), an external-review grant, or a verify share link.
findings.legalImpact: Bearer capabilities to private evidence disclosure are retained in operational logs beyond their revocation window.
findings.reproduction: GET /v1/external-intake/<token> -> onResponse logs {url: '/v1/external-intake/<token>'} at info ('request.completed'); TOKEN_IN_PATH covers only collaboration-team-invites, teams/invites, collaboration-teams/invites. Same for /public/verify/pvs_..., /v1/external-review/access/<token>, /v1/org-invites/<token>/accept.
findings.expected: Redact every :token path parameter by route pattern (or log req.routeOptions.url instead of req.url).
findings.rootCause: Redaction is a hand-maintained regex list rather than derived from route parameters.
findings.remediation: Log the route pattern plus non-secret params; or extend redaction to all routes whose pattern contains :token and to /public/verify/pvs_*.
findings.requiredTests: Inject each token route through app.inject with a captured logger; assert the token never appears.
findings.runtimeProbe: buildServer() with a pino destination stream; app.inject GET /v1/external-intake/abc123secret; grep captured lines for abc123secret.

findings.title: Extension capture tokens have no AuthenticatedSession row, so organization session policy (mandatory SSO/MFA, context policy), role session-timeout and per-session revocation never apply; authMethod is hard-coded SOCIAL_OAUTH
findings.userImpact: An organization that mandates SSO or short reviewer/contributor timeouts cannot bind extension captures into its workspace to that policy; the token is invisible in the user's session list and cannot be revoked individually.
findings.legalImpact: Captures may enter an organization workspace under an authentication that the organization's policy would refuse.
findings.securityImpact: Policy bypass for a 1h capture-scoped token (bounded by scope allowlist and ALL_FOR_USER revocation).
findings.reproduction: Token minted by signJwt (random sid) with no recordAuthenticatedSession; requireAuth reads authenticatedSession by sid -> null -> teamId null -> the gateSecurityAction/evaluateOrgContextForSession block and enforceSessionTimeoutPolicy are no-ops. authorizeOrFail (middleware/authorize.ts) does not evaluate org SSO/MFA policy. The token claims authMethod SOCIAL_OAUTH regardless of how the user authenticated.
findings.observed: Org policy anchored to a session row the extension token never has.
findings.expected: Record an AuthenticatedSession for the extension token anchored to the workspace it will capture into (or evaluate org context policy per target workspace), and carry the parent session's real provenance.
findings.rootCause: Extension OAuth reuses signJwt but not the session-inventory write that every other login path performs.
findings.remediation: Call recordAuthenticatedSession at token exchange with the authorizing session's provenance; evaluate evaluateOrgContextForSession for the target team in authorizeDirectCapture.
findings.requiredTests: Org with requireSaml; password-authenticated member mints extension token; POST /v1/capture/direct-sessions for the org team -> refused.

findings.title: Production CORS reflects any *.vercel.app origin and three localhost origins with credentials:true
findings.securityImpact: Defense-in-depth: any attacker-deployed *.vercel.app page is an allowed credentialed origin. Currently mitigated because the session cookie is SameSite=Lax (not sent on cross-site fetch) and bearer tokens are not ambient; a future SameSite=None cookie would make it exploitable.
findings.reproduction: isProovraOrigin returns true for value.endsWith('.vercel.app'); REQUIRED_ORIGINS merges http://localhost:3000/3001/8081 into the production allowlist.
findings.expected: Only the project's own preview domain pattern (e.g. proovra-*.vercel.app with team slug) and no localhost in production.
findings.rootCause: Preview convenience left in the production policy.
findings.remediation: Restrict to exact preview pattern; drop localhost when NODE_ENV=production.
findings.requiredTests: Preflight from https://evil.vercel.app in production -> no ACAO.

findings.title: Public Verify's per-IP limiter and the capture/presign limiters use the default process bound, so they are per-replica and fall back to memory during a Redis outage
findings.securityImpact: The anonymous verify surface's enumeration bound scales with replica count; legacy UUID links are the only guessable identifier (share tokens are 256-bit).
findings.reproduction: enforceRateLimit({key:'ratelimit:verify:ip:...'}) and enforceDistinctClientLimit(...) are called without bound:'global' (default 'process'), unlike external-intake.routes.ts:180,197.
findings.rootCause: Global bound applied to intake/auth but not verify.
findings.remediation: Pass bound:'global' on the verify IP and per-evidence buckets.
findings.requiredTests: Existing rate-limit unit tests with bound assertion.
